why: Judge 1 is right; I confirm each step. Step 1: a CELL resource has a cell count fixed when it is defined, 16 by default (V5-PRIMITIVE; SPACE P `fixN`). Step 2: 16 cells give 7 to 15 writers' worth under skew (E-18, B4), below F_w = 64, so the resource must grow past 16 to reach the floor. Step 3: its only growth is a re-key into a new generation with more cells, and E-17 part 1 says "the count is chosen per re-key". Step 4: nothing in the row chooses it: its P cell has no `+ rule`, its C is `self` (healing only, no planner), and SPACE's ladder keeps the automatic grow rule as one more mechanism on the slot path, outside CELL's count of about 3. So a person picks a shard count to grow, at define time or at a re-key; a rule that picks it would be another row's option. That answers judge 2's open point (who picks). If the user lowers F_w to 7 or less, the default 16 is enough and no count is needed: met.

Judge 2 is right; I confirm each step in v4's own records. Step 1: v4 has the cascade and its one importer (CLAUDE.md), so that half holds. Step 2: every v4 server says its cluster values (heartbeat.ms, replicas, methods, the validation text, the ring) in its first frame, and two servers whose values differ refuse to link (README, the scope note; STATUS.md, open limits). Step 3: a change made online means one member has the new value while another has the old; the two refuse each other, so the cluster splits until every member and client is stopped and started. STATUS.md calls this "refused by design" (DESIGN-DOOR section 4). OPS-03 asks that cluster keys change online. Judge 1 names the same fact and leaves it open, but closing it needs a new mechanism, which is not v4 as it is.

Judge 2 is right; I confirm each step. Step 1: OPS-05 asks that a roll across two kernel builds works, with new behaviour held back by a cluster version until every member is new. Step 2: v4 has no cluster version, and its decision V4-14 says mixed versions are unsupported (STATUS.md). Step 3: its code makes a mixed pair refuse each other on purpose: the door's proof label was raised so that an old and a new member both fail `bad-proof` (kernel/door.ts; DECISIONS, V4-55), and an old feeder strands its clients' writes (DECISIONS, V4-43). Step 4: so in a roll across such builds the first restarted member is refused by the rest, and the roll test fails; the supported way is to stop every member (README, "Mixed versions do not link").

Judge 2 is right; I confirm each step. Step 1: v4's door admits a peer only if it proves the one configured secret; there is no second key and no window (DESIGN-DOOR: "No rotation key"; "no revocation, no rotation window"). Step 2: so a member on the new secret and a member on the old one refuse each other, and the client key is derived from the same secret. Step 3: changing the secret is a full stop and start of every member and client (README, the `secret` row; STATUS.md, open limits). OPS-06 asks for rotation with no downtime, and its own sentence says v4 cannot. v4 also has no TLS, no tokens with claims and no admin key.

why: Judge 1 is right. E-22 ran each seed twice in 200 worlds with the same trace hash, with the four calls on the world's clock; writer time is the median (A-23), and E-21's closing line names ISR among the rows it moves up on TEST-02. closes: A rerun bench against a stand-in log, or a fresh stream per rerun. Not planned: a reference row.

why: Judge 1 is right. LANE holds one offset per lane (O `off`), so in log mode the shuffle must keep each lane's own order for a cursor to stay exact (E-22, API-NOTES C7), and two partitions of one lane are never shuffled apart. Judge 2 says they never part, but the row moves key ranges between lanes in a later phase (SPACE 4.2: "range moves later"; E-17b priced that move), and that parts them. CELL and SPLIT hold the same O `off` and are open by both judges on this ground.
closes: A shuffle inside a lane that keeps O `off` cursors exact, run on the 22 examples and the planted app; or the row states that a lane's range never moves.

why: Judge 2 is right. E-22's sim checkers ran over a modelled log, so they show the layers above a core, not the core. Judge 1's carry-over is reasoned, not run. SLOG and OBJ are open by both judges on the same ground: their own log never met a checker.
closes: E-46's adapter around the raft-rs kernel, with Knossos and Porcupine on its histories, from phase 1.
